name: Robert L. Glass

early_history_summary: Robert L. Glass began in aerospace computing in 1954 at North American Aviation, then Aerojet-General and Boeing, building software tools for applications specialists. evidence_summary: Glass is a pioneering software practitioner-writer born in 1932 who entered computing in 1954. Career start alone is not treated as a material age-26 milestone under the rubric; his widely cited books, columns, and ACM Fellow recognition arrived well after age 26.

name: Michael Baum (entrepreneur)
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded Reality Online (stock-market modeling software) around Drexel graduation in 1985 at age ~23; the company was Venrock-backed and later acquired by Reuters (sources cite 1987–1989).
early_history_summary: Born in Philadelphia in 1962, Baum studied computer science at Drexel (BS 1985), switching toward CS after Steve Jobs visited campus with the Macintosh. In his final year he co-founded Reality Online with his brother and a Wharton classmate; after its acquisition he earned a Wharton MBA and built multiple later startups culminating in Splunk (2003).
family_context_summary: Philadelphia-area roots; first-generation college student per Drexel coverage. Older brother was a Wharton student and co-founder of Reality Online.
parent_family_domain_summary: Parents named Mardell A. Baum and Richard L. Baum, Sr. on Wikipedia; no clear parental tech-domain transfer documented beyond sibling co-founding.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Drexel co-op, sibling cofounder, Macintosh campus wave, Reality Online, serial founder
evidence_summary: Baum co-founded Reality Online at ~23 with family and campus peers during the early PC/Mac era, secured Venrock funding, and exited to Reuters before age ~27. He later founded multiple venture-backed companies including Splunk (IPO; later Cisco acquisition ~$28B). Early leverage was technical CS training, sibling cofounder, and early microcomputing exposure rather than inherited capital.
starting_point: Born May 28, 1962 in Philadelphia; first-generation college student who studied CS at Drexel and launched a startup with his brother while still in school.
current_position: Serial entrepreneur and investor; former founding CEO of Splunk (acquired by Cisco for ~$28B); proprietor of Château de Pommard; leads founder-focused efforts including FOUNDER.org / Yope Foundation.

trajectory.event: Co-founded Reality Online (stock-market modeling software) around Drexel graduation; later Venrock-backed and acquired by Reuters.
Reality Online acquisition period completed; pursued Wharton MBA and continued serial entrepreneurship.
Co-founded Splunk with Rob Das and Erik Swan as founding CEO, pioneering machine-data search analytics.
Splunk IPO; company became a major public big-data/security software firm.
Acquired Château de Pommard in Burgundy and shifted into wine proprietorship alongside founder education.
Cisco announced acquisition of Splunk for about $28 billion in cash.

name: Naomi Gleit
category: Product executive / Meta Head of Product
milestone_by_age_26: Joined Facebook on July 18, 2005 (her 22nd birthday) as employee #29 shortly after the company hit 1 million users; wrote her Stanford senior thesis on Facebook and became a core early growth product leader.
early_history_summary: Raised in New York City by an Asian-American 'tiger mom' (computer programmer) and a Jewish father (immigration lawyer). Studied Science, Technology, and Society at Stanford, wrote her thesis on why Facebook beat Club Nexus on campus, then talked her way into Facebook as employee #29 and later led growth, social good, and product.
family_context_summary: Raised in NYC by an Asian-American mother described as a tiger mom and computer programmer, and a Jewish father who was an immigration lawyer; ferried to ballet, piano, karate, Chinese, and Hebrew school.
parent_family_domain_summary: Mother was a computer programmer, providing some early tech-domain proximity; father practiced immigration law. Not a startup or product-management apprenticeship, but STEM/discipline culture at home.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Stanford, Facebook employee 29, growth team, social networks wave, thesis on Facebook
evidence_summary: Gleit entered Facebook at 22 as employee #29 after a Stanford thesis on the product itself, then became a defining growth PM and later Meta Head of Product—second-longest-tenured employee after Zuckerberg. Advantages include Stanford STS training, early domain immersion via thesis, and joining the social-network structural wave at the right moment; family provided disciplined dual-culture upbringing and a programmer mother, not startup capital.
starting_point: Born July 18, 1983; raised in New York City by an Asian-American computer-programmer mother and a Jewish immigration-lawyer father.
current_position: Head of Product at Meta Platforms; Meta’s longest-serving employee after Mark Zuckerberg.

trajectory.event: Joined Facebook as employee #29 on her birthday (July 18), after a Stanford senior thesis on why Facebook won on campus.
Moved into product management on Facebook’s growth team under Chamath Palihapitiya, focusing on global user expansion.
As senior director of growth, engagement and mobile, helped scale Facebook past 1 billion users.
Helped launch Facebook Safety Check and later led the company’s social-good product efforts.
Serving as Head of Product at Meta following the company’s rebrand from Facebook.

name: Slava Akhmechet
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded RethinkDB and joined Y Combinator (S09) in May 2009 at about age 26 (born Ukraine; moved to NYC at ~13 in 1996), dropping out of a Stony Brook computational neuroscience PhD to build a distributed database startup.
early_history_summary: Born in Ukraine and immigrated to New York City around age 13 in 1996; programmed from a young age. Earned a BS in computer science at Stony Brook (2001–2004), worked as a systems engineer in finance (Thomson Reuters, MarketAxess), began a computational neuroscience PhD, then left to found RethinkDB with YC in 2009.
family_context_summary: Immigrated from Ukraine to New York City with parents around age 13 in 1996; family background otherwise not detailed in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: immigrant, early programming, Stony Brook, YC S09, finance systems engineering, RethinkDB
evidence_summary: Akhmechet combined deep systems/database skills from finance engineering and academic CS with YC network access to found RethinkDB at ~26. Immigrant constraint and early self-taught programming are documented; family domain/capital advantages are not. Company later shut down and tech was absorbed via open source / Stripe-era path; he later worked at Stripe and Microsoft Azure.
starting_point: Born in Ukraine circa 1983; moved with parents to New York City around age 13 in 1996 and programmed from childhood.
current_position: Engineering at Microsoft Azure on distributed data services; previously at Stripe; co-founder/CEO of RethinkDB (2009–2016).

trajectory.event: Completed BS in computer science at Stony Brook and began industry systems engineering roles in finance.
Co-founded RethinkDB, joined Y Combinator S09, and left a computational neuroscience PhD to build a distributed database.
Grew RethinkDB as open-source realtime database company with venture funding and developer community adoption.
RethinkDB company shut down; open-sourced remaining assets and later joined Stripe in product/engineering.
Joined Microsoft engineering, working on Azure distributed data services.
